summary: Sourcehut provides a web-based interface for managing source code repositories using Git. It operates entirely without JavaScript, focusing on a lightweight approach to software development and project management. The platform is written in Go and distributed under the GPL-2.0 licence.
goodFor: It suits developers who prefer minimal, text-heavy web interfaces that load quickly and function without client-side scripting. It is also an option for teams wanting to self-host their version control infrastructure under a copyleft licence.
watchOut: The lack of official tagged releases and the unrated maintenance activity suggest potential risks regarding long-term support and stability. Evaluating whether the feature set meets your specific project management workflow is necessary before adoption.
deployNotes: As a Go application, it typically compiles into a single binary that you can run behind a standard reverse proxy like Nginx or Caddy to handle TLS termination. You will also usually need to provision a separate database and ensure persistent storage for your Git repositories.
